title: Natural tap and doing one step several ways
summary: Green explains he liked bare feet and demonstrates one step done several ways, circling and the Replay.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: What kind of dancing did you do?

Well, I did natural tap dancing, see, because I was a natural dancer, see. See, I finally had got on some taps. See, I was the kind of a person that didn't like to wear shoes -- I like to have -- I liked nakedness -- I liked my feet to be naked, you know. Because I could feel the weather and all these tings, you know. And I'll give you an idea. You know when they have, what they call trackers, like in the law -- they would -- this is in the outdoors, open air, you know. And if they was trailing someone, like the Mounties in Canada would say, "Always gets their man," the Mounty, you know. He had to know how to track, you see. Like some hunter or something, you know. Well, I tried to educate myself in those kind of degrees, you see, and tried to learn how to be additional -- like, do one thing more than one way. Do it several ways, but it would be the same portion -- or partiality, however you would say, you see. But it was needed in those days.
Well, I'm curious to know how you did that. In other words, what I'd like you to do is give me an example by tapping of how you took one thing and did it a number
of different ways.
Yes.
Can you show me that?
Oh, easily. This is from "Repeat Performance." It's a tap dance (unintelligible), see. That's the same step several different tap ways. Here we go. These are the (unintelligible).
(dancing)
That's twice. Then -- (dancing) Did you get that?
Sure I did.
It goes on and on until you began to circling, see. That circling -- circling is this. (dancing) That's circling.
Why did you call that circling?
Because tap dancing was always making up satire in sound, you see, satirical in sound, see.
You're doing the same rhythm but I see you're doing different foot work in every one -- in all those changes. Very interesting.
Yes.
You want to continue?

Well, I could, I could. I could do the other thing, what they call Replays -- Replay. They did that and that was in "Happy Days are Here Again," you see. So, I shall (unintelligible) be demonstrative. Come on feet, (unintelligible).
(dancing)
: Beautiful.
Maybe I went over some bumpy roads, but the lumps was all there.
(Recording interruption)
